To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new approach for the computation of the k-th level of an arrangement and the order-k Voronoï diagram, that we can solve these problems with randomized algorithms that run in time O(nk) and O(nk log n), respectively, where k is the order, n is the size of the problem and k and n are of the same order of magnitude.

(1) the Amk-level of an arrangement of n x-monotone curves in the plane can be computed in expected time O(nk + n log n), and (2) the k-level of such an arrangement can be computed in O(k(n-k + log n) + n log n) time.
the Amk-level can be computed efficiently for any k, and that the order-k Voroni diagram can be computed in O(nk) time for any fixed k.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of computing levels and higher order Voronoi diagrams.
the problem of constructing levels in arrangements and with computing higher order Voronoi diagrams.
the following problem: Given an arrangement A of n objects, and a number k, how can one construct the k-level, i.e., the set of points of A which are at least at distance k from all other points?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have a randomized algorithm with expected time complexity O(k(n-k)n + n log3) for computing the order k Voronoi diagram for n points in the Euclidean plane, where k is the order of the Voronoi diagram.
our algorithms are simple, fast and efficient.
the k-level can be computed in optimal time for any k = o(n), and that for any constant k the k-level can always be computed in optimal expected time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give a randomized incremental construction of the Amk-level for any fixed k, which is the first such result in the literature.

our algorithms for computing the k-level in arrangements of lines in the plane and of planes in $\Reels^3$ run in time O(nk+n log3 n), and for the order-k Voroni diagram of n points run in time O(k(nk)log n+n log3 n).
the Amk-level can be computed in expected time O(nk+n log n) in the plane and O(nk3/2+n log3 n) in space, for any fixed constant k.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in many cases, it suffices to consider only the Amk-level of an arrangement in order to obtain a good algorithm for computing its k-level.
we can compute higher order Voronoi diagrams in the same time complexity as lower order diagrams, which is not possible with the standard incremental approach.
we show that the Amk-level can be constructed in the same time as the Am-level for all k.
